availableCommands.name: run-workflow
availableCommands.description: How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don't use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).

availableCommands.name: swarm
availableCommands.description: (Preview & Quota Heavy) Run a swarm: several agents working in parallel on one task, each in its own conversation, collaborating through a shared message board. Use when the work splits into pieces that can be done at the same time, or when a second pair of eyes should check the first pair's work.

content.text:
Initial hypothesis: README's title should be retrievable from the file contents. Exploring the file to extract the title.

Reading the README yielded no immediately obvious title format. Considering the possibility of a header structure or project naming convention.

The prompt explicitly asks for a title from the README after a test suite run, implying the test results are relevant to finding the title. The mnemonic instruction focuses on remembering information across sessions, suggesting the title is something important to retain. It's possible the test results or the context of a successful test run might provide a clue or direct link to the README title.

The transient test run result ("42 tests passed") is deemed irrelevant for long-term memory. It does not qualify as a convention, command, decision, correction, or preference. The focus is on retrieving project conventions and decisions, and the ephemeral test result is noise, not durable knowledge. The search for existing project information will take precedence.

The `README.md` was read, revealing the title "alpha". This satisfies the one-line requirement and provides a direct answer to the prompt. The ephemeral nature of the test run and the specific question focus exclude the test results from being a relevant memory cue. The file link is now constructed in GitHub style with the `file://` scheme to satisfy the explicit instruction.
